patch.value:
## Rationale

This repository's own `.agents/pm` workspace is the product's most-used deployment and its primary defect-discovery mechanism: nearly every agent-UX defect in the tracker was found by using pm to manage pm. That mechanism only covers capabilities the maintainer workspace actually exercises. A shipped capability nobody here uses has no live user at all, so its defects surface at an external adopter instead of in CI.

## Measured coverage (2026-07-25, 2,022 items)

Exercised: 11 built-in types, 1 custom type (Story), Plans (21), Milestones (7), claims/releases, comments/notes/learnings, files/docs/tests links, structured deps across 9 edge kinds, history redact/repair/compact, merge drivers, telemetry, graph analytics.

Never exercised:
- **custom fields: 0** — `pm schema add-field` ships and the workspace declares no field, so field validation, projection, and merge behaviour for custom fields are untested by dogfooding.
- **custom statuses: 0** — 6 built-ins only; per-type workflows unexercised (pm-z5nb owns completing that capability).
- **project profiles: 3 shipped (agile, ops, research), 0 applied** — profile apply/lint has no dogfood signal.
- **Meeting: 0 items, Event: 0 items, Reminder: 1** — the calendar surface (`pm meet`/`pm event`/`pm remind`) is effectively unused, which is exactly how GH-450 (`--duration 5m` parses as 5 months, pm-jkjt) survived: a silent wrong-data defect in a type nobody creates.
- extension-contributed types, custom relationship kinds, and `--type-option` values likewise carry no live usage.

## Deliverable

Not "adopt every feature" — adoption for its own sake would pollute the tracker. The deliverable is **visibility plus a decision per capability**:

1. A capability-usage report derived from the workspace and the runtime schema/contract tables: for each shipped, agent-reachable capability, when it was last exercised in this workspace (from history), or never.
2. A disposition for every never-exercised capability, recorded on the owning item: **adopt** (use it here for real work), **cover** (a scenario test carries the load dogfooding would have), or **waive** (documented reason, e.g. a capability that only makes sense in a foreign domain).
3. A ratchet: the never-exercised-and-undispositioned set may only shrink. A new capability ships with its disposition, so the gap cannot silently regrow — the same shrinking-allowlist shape as the eslint-suppression and unaudited-mutation ratchets.

## Relationship to neighbours

- pm-xgcp18 proves documented examples execute; this proves shipped capabilities are exercised by real tracked work. Complementary, not overlapping.
- pm-k6t4yb registers enforced gates; this registers exercised capabilities.
- pm-z5nb completes the schema-customization capability; this measures whether we then use it.
- pm-rtn5h6 turns escaped defects into gates; "never dogfooded" is the leading indicator that predicts where those escapes come from.
Capability dogfood coverage ratchet: every shipped capability is exercised by real tracked work here, or carries a recorded cover-or-waive disposition

Measure which shipped, agent-reachable pm capabilities the maintainer workspace actually exercises (custom fields, custom statuses, profiles, calendar types and extension-contributed surfaces are currently at zero), require an adopt/cover/waive disposition for each never-exercised capability, and ratchet the undispositioned set downward so new capabilities cannot ship without one.

A report derived from the runtime schema and contract tables plus workspace history lists every shipped agent-reachable capability with its last-exercised timestamp in this workspace or never; every never-exercised capability carries a recorded disposition of adopt, cover (named scenario test), or waive (documented reason) on its owning item; a gate fails when a capability is neither exercised nor dispositioned, and the undispositioned set is shrinking-only so a newly shipped capability must arrive with its disposition; the currently-zero set (custom fields, custom statuses, applied profiles, Meeting/Event items, extension-contributed types and relationship kinds) is dispositioned as the first pass; the report is token-budgeted and runnable in CI

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Add to the never-exercised capability list: the release field. It is plumbed across create --release, update --release, list --release, and list --filter-release-missing, and the changelog generator can bucket a release window by it independently of any timestamp. Zero of 2,068 items in this workspace carry a value. The dogfood gap here is not cosmetic — the unused capability is exactly what would make release attribution immutable, which is why it is filed as a defect in its own right under pm-pcys9n rather than only as a coverage entry.

author: harness:claude-code
message: The release field is the never-exercised capability whose absence has a downstream governance cost

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Correction to the preceding note on this item, 2026-07-26: the claim that zero items carry a release value was measured through pm list --json, which does not project the field, and is wrong. Reading the item files directly gives 469 items with a release value — all terminal, fourteen distinct values, exactly one of which matches a real git tag. No active item carries one. The dogfood conclusion changes shape rather than disappearing: release is not an unexercised capability, it is a capability exercised with archival placeholder values (archive-2026q2 on 282 items) that cannot match a release window. The same pattern covers reviewer, sprint, environment, definition_of_ready and customer_impact and is owned as a data-quality defect by pm-pj2isb. For this item's purposes the useful distinction is between a capability never invoked and a capability invoked with values that carry no information — the ratchet should count the second as uncovered.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Dogfood observation recorded 2026-07-26 from a large governance pass, useful as a datapoint for the adopt/cover/waive ledger this item keeps.

Two capabilities moved from never-exercised to exercised at scale today, both through update-many rather than through their own surface:
- The release field went from 469 items carrying values that matched no real tag (a legacy taxonomy reading as adopted while behaving as absent) to 1,782 terminal items carrying a real tag. It is now a load-bearing attribution key rather than an unused column.
- update-many itself ran 68 times over explicit id allowlists and once per enriched item, which is the first bulk use of the checkpointed path against the real tracker at this volume. Zero failures across 1,781 stamped items.

Still never exercised on this workspace and therefore still open on this item's ledger: custom schema types, custom statuses, applied project profiles, and Meeting or Event items. Worth noting the asymmetry — the fields we do not use are cheap to adopt, but the reason none of them are used is that this repository is a software project and its archetype is the default one. A genuine test of the schema surface needs a workspace whose archetype is not software, which is what pm-w89s universality and pm-g608fc domain packs are for. Suggest this item's ledger distinguish "unused because unnecessary here" from "unused because unreachable", since only the second is a defect signal.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Lifecycle and type occupancy measured 2026-07-28 across the complete corpus: 2,144 items and all 40,343 history entries.

Declared statuses are six: draft, open, in_progress, blocked, closed, canceled. Status values ever WRITTEN in any recorded patch, with counts:

  open 2471, closed 2213, in_progress 1894, canceled 13, blocked 11, draft 0.

draft has NEVER been written, not once, in the entire recorded history of the flagship workspace. blocked has been written 11 times against 6,602 status writes, which is 0.17 percent, and no item currently occupies it. So of six declared lifecycle states, one has zero lifetime occupancy and a second is effectively vestigial while a parallel edge-derived mechanism computes the same concept and is what next, context and list-blocked actually consult.

This is worth an explicit disposition rather than drift, because both states carry surface area: pm list-draft and pm list-blocked are rendered commands, both statuses appear in every status enum an agent must read, and blocked in particular is a second, disagreeing representation of blockedness whose authoritative form is the dependency graph. The choices are to adopt each state deliberately with a documented meaning, to mark it as a compatibility-only value that the product does not itself use, or to retire it. Doing nothing keeps paying the surface cost for states the product never enters.

Type occupancy on the same corpus: 17 declared types, of which 8 hold zero items. Card, Changeset, TwinAsset, TwinFacility and VcsRef are extension-provided and their emptiness in a bare workspace is expected. The three BUILTIN types with no or near-zero occupancy are Event 0, Meeting 0 and Reminder 1. Those are first-party types the product ships and the flagship workspace has never meaningfully used.

Same disposition question, same three options. Recording here because this item owns adopt-cover-waive per never-exercised capability, and these are the two largest remaining unexercised first-party surfaces after custom fields, custom statuses and applied profiles.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Dogfood census re-run 2026-07-29 against pm schema list: custom types 0, custom statuses 0, custom fields 0, so the workspace still runs entirely on the six builtin statuses and zero declared extensions to the schema. Item-type coverage from pm stats is Task 643, Issue 640, Feature 398, Chore 276, Epic 87, Decision 63, Story 53, Plan 22, Milestone 7, Reminder 1, and zero for Card, Changeset, Event, Meeting, TwinAsset, TwinFacility and VcsRef. So seven declared item types have never been instantiated once in 2,193 items, and the three capability families this item named as never-exercised - custom fields, custom statuses, applied profiles - remain at exactly zero after another month. The Reminder count of 1 is the interesting row: it is the only type with a single instance, which means the calendar shortcut family has been exercised precisely once and never since. Worth citing when the adopt-cover-waive decision is made, because a type with one instance and a type with zero are different arguments: one was tried and abandoned, the other was never reachable enough to try.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Capability adoption census 2026-07-29, for the adopt-cover-waive ledger this item owns.

Item types with zero instances after 2,196 items: Card, Changeset, Event, Meeting, TwinAsset, TwinFacility, VcsRef. Reminder has exactly one. Statuses: draft is still written zero times across the whole history, and blocked and in_progress are both zero at rest right now, though in_progress is genuinely transient rather than unexercised. Custom item types, custom statuses, custom fields and applied schema profiles remain at zero in this workspace.

Newly shipped surfaces and their adoption in this repository's own tracking: workspace snapshot has never been used against the real tracker, only in sandboxes; eval runs against a four-query set and is wired into no pipeline, tracked as pm-b2hc4x; duplicates has no recorded use even though this repository's own agent rules require a duplicate check before creating work; item mutate has no recorded use even though every session performs sequences of create and update that it exists to make atomic.

What the census argues for the ledger's shape. Three of the four newest capabilities are unused by the project that ships them, and in each case the reason is discoverability rather than unsuitability - the operation an agent is told to perform has a shorter, older spelling that does not use the new primitive. So the ratchet should record, per capability, not only adopt-cover-waive but which existing spelling an agent reaches for instead, because that is the field that tells whether non-adoption is a gap in the capability or a gap in the guidance.
